title: Amadeus
selection_rationale: Patronage, class, opera, envy, and the modern myth of genius.
carry_question: Does the film show us Mozart — or what later centuries wanted Mozart to mean?
bridge: Rewind next to Bach; later compare genius with institution in TÁR.
source_status: Visual prototype v0.2 — awaiting owner review

title: Chronicle of Anna Magdalena Bach
selection_rationale: Music as skilled labor within church, court, household, and civic institution.
carry_question: What becomes visible when biography stops explaining the music?
bridge: Compare Bach's institutional world with TÁR's modern orchestra.

title: Mahler
selection_rationale: Late empire, Jewish identity, interiority, memory, and the artist as psychological battleground.
carry_question: What happens when an artwork becomes a container for the artist's inner life?
bridge: Leads toward Schoenberg/modernism and later institutional Mahler in TÁR.

title: The Blue Angel
functions: Performance; Cultural Context; Early Sound Cinema
selection_rationale: A film made inside Weimar culture: cabaret, sexuality, performer persona, and sound-era stardom.
carry_question: What can contemporary entertainment reveal that later reconstruction cannot?

title: Cabaret
functions: Cultural Context; Historical Commentary; Anachronistic Reconstruction
selection_rationale: Later generations use invented musical language to interpret a political collapse they know is coming.
carry_question: What can hindsight hear that people living through history cannot?
bridge: Compare with actual Weimar recordings and The Blue Angel.

title: The Sound of Music
selection_rationale: American musical theater becomes the global imagined soundtrack for pre-Anschluss Austria.
carry_question: Can invented music become more culturally 'authentic' than historical music?
bridge: Pair with The Third Man as competing cinematic memories of Austria.

title: The Third Man
selection_rationale: The imperial city in ruins receives a new vernacular sonic identity through Anton Karas's zither.
carry_question: Why might one small vernacular instrument tell the truth about a city better than a full orchestra?

title: Wings of Desire
functions: Cultural Context; Popular Music; City Portrait
selection_rationale: Memory, urban space, division, international artists, and post-punk subculture occupy the same historical city.
carry_question: Can a city's wounds become part of its creative infrastructure?
bridge: Opens later routes into post-punk/electronic and transnational urban music.

title: The Piano Teacher
selection_rationale: The classical canon survives through conservatory culture, discipline, pedagogy, and repression.
carry_question: When does mastery liberate — and when does it confine?
bridge: Bridge to Play Canon Leonard/Illich and to institutional critique in TÁR.

title: TÁR
functions: Institution; Fictional Artist; Cultural Critique; Performance
selection_rationale: The composer-hero gives way to conductor, orchestra, recording industry, boards, reputation, and cultural authority.
carry_question: Who owns a musical tradition once its creators are dead but its institutions remain powerful?
bridge: Explicit doorway to Course II through Tchaikovsky Symphony No. 6.
